client: Hi Luna, I've been feeling really troubled lately about my relationship with my parents. I can't shake off this guilt that I'm not a good enough child to them. I constantly think about all the things I should have done differently or better. Sometimes, I wonder if therapy can really help me work through these feelings or if I'm just going to keep going in circles.
therapist:
Hi there! It's great to hear from you, though I can sense that you're feeling quite troubled about your relationship with your parents. It sounds like there's a lot of guilt weighing on you, and you're reflecting on what you could have done differently. Those feelings can be really heavy to carry.

I also noticed that you might be feeling uncertain about the effectiveness of therapy. It’s completely understandable to wonder if it will help you break free from these cycles of thought. 

I wonder if there are deeper feelings beneath the surface of that guilt. Sometimes, when we feel like we haven't lived up to expectations, it can stir up other emotions too. How do you feel when you think about your relationship with your parents? What do you think might be contributing to that sense of not being "good enough"?
vocal_descriptors: very high pitch, soft-spoken, moderate-paced speech

therapist:

therapist:

I hear you saying that keeping everything inside feels like a safer option, but I wonder if part of you is also feeling more overwhelmed by these feelings than you're letting on. Facing those emotions can be daunting, especially when you're worried about what you might uncover.
